name: Implement programs and scripts
definition: Write and check executable logic for a specified software or automation task.

FOUNDATION.text: Trace branching and collection operations for a small order calculator
Identify boundary inputs and explain the expected result

INTERMEDIATE.text: Implement decomposed pricing logic with explicit error handling
Verify empty, invalid and boundary cases without changing the stated rules

ADVANCED.text: Evaluate alternative implementations under changing discount policies
Justify complexity and maintainability trade-offs using failure cases

excludedScope: Framework deployment and architecture selection

name: Manage source changes with version control
definition: Record and review source changes so a tested version can be identified and recovered.

FOUNDATION.text: Explain commits, branches and working-tree changes
Recover a mistaken local edit without losing unrelated work

INTERMEDIATE.text: Resolve a conflicting feature change while preserving both intended behaviors
Prepare a reviewable history and identify the tested revision

ADVANCED.text: Design a branching and hotfix strategy for concurrent releases
Evaluate rollback and traceability risks across maintained versions

excludedScope: Build pipeline authoring and application debugging

name: Translate requirements into verifiable changes
definition: Connect a stated user or service need to a bounded implementation and explicit checks.

FOUNDATION.text: Identify actors, inputs and outputs in a small user request
Write observable acceptance examples including one failure case

INTERMEDIATE.text: Resolve ambiguities in a multi-step user workflow
Define testable business rules and boundaries before implementation

ADVANCED.text: Reconcile conflicting functional and quality constraints
Prioritize a bounded release with traceable acceptance and explicit residual risk

excludedScope: UI styling and implementation of the whole feature

name: Deploy a controlled software release
definition: Apply an agreed deployment procedure and verify the released service and rollback path.

FOUNDATION.text: Explain configuration, artifact and health-check roles in a release
Identify the rollback point in a supplied deployment procedure

INTERMEDIATE.text: Plan a reproducible application rollout with environment-specific configuration
Verify service health and define rollback triggers

ADVANCED.text: Evaluate staged rollout alternatives under migration and availability constraints
Specify evidence for safe rollback when versions coexist

excludedScope: Cloud platform administration and continuous-integration pipeline design

name: design user interface
definition: Specify user interface structure and interactions for a user task.

FOUNDATION.text: Identify interface states and navigation for a simple user task
Explain the purpose of clear labels and actionable feedback

INTERMEDIATE.text: Specify interaction states for an interrupted multi-step task
Resolve navigation and error-recovery ambiguities with a flow model

ADVANCED.text: Compare interaction alternatives for conflicting user needs
Justify recovery and consistency decisions across complex workflows

excludedScope: Semantic HTML implementation and visual branding

name: Implement accessible user interfaces
definition: Implement interfaces that support keyboard and assistive technology use.

FOUNDATION.text: Explain semantic controls, accessible names and keyboard order
Identify inaccessible interactions in a small form

INTERMEDIATE.text: Specify keyboard and focus behavior for a dialog and validation flow
Check accessible names and dynamic feedback against observable criteria

ADVANCED.text: Evaluate accessibility trade-offs in a complex interactive widget
Design a verification strategy across input methods and assistive use

excludedScope: Full accessibility certification and purely visual layout work

name: design application interfaces
definition: Define interfaces through which application components exchange information.

FOUNDATION.text: Explain request, response and error conventions for a resource API
Select suitable operations and response meanings for basic CRUD

INTERMEDIATE.text: Specify pagination, validation and repeat-request behavior for an API
Check examples for consistent success and failure contracts

ADVANCED.text: Evaluate versioning and compatibility strategies for changing consumers
Justify idempotency and failure semantics under partial completion

excludedScope: Database schema design and UI implementation

name: use query languages
definition: Retrieve and manipulate data using a query language.

FOUNDATION.text: Explain filtering, joining and aggregation on related tables
Predict the result of a query with missing or duplicate rows

INTERMEDIATE.text: Construct queries for grouped business reports with explicit null handling
Check result correctness against a small reference dataset

ADVANCED.text: Compare equivalent query formulations under skewed data and access constraints
Justify an optimization while preserving result semantics

excludedScope: Database administration and transaction-isolation design

name: integrate system components
definition: Connect components and verify their combined behaviour.

FOUNDATION.text: Identify producer, consumer and exchanged data in an integration
Explain how a failed dependency affects a user operation

INTERMEDIATE.text: Specify component coordination with timeouts and partial-failure handling
Define contract and integration checks for the combined workflow

ADVANCED.text: Evaluate recovery strategies for repeated or out-of-order messages
Justify consistency and coupling trade-offs across service boundaries

excludedScope: Individual function implementation and API naming conventions alone

name: debug software
definition: Locate and correct causes of software defects.

FOUNDATION.text: Reproduce a defect from a bounded input and observed output
Distinguish symptoms from a testable causal hypothesis

INTERMEDIATE.text: Trace a failure across UI, API and persistence boundaries
Verify the smallest justified correction with a regression case

ADVANCED.text: Evaluate competing explanations for an intermittent production-like fault
Design discriminating observations and validate a fix under recurrence conditions

excludedScope: Broad monitoring infrastructure and feature redesign

name: perform software unit testing
definition: Verify individual units of software with repeatable automated checks.

FOUNDATION.text: Explain assertions, test isolation and boundary cases
Identify useful tests for a pure validation function

INTERMEDIATE.text: Design deterministic unit tests around service collaborators
Verify error behavior without coupling tests to private implementation details

ADVANCED.text: Evaluate a unit-test suite for blind spots and brittle doubles
Select high-value cases for complex state transitions and mutation risks

excludedScope: Full end-to-end browser testing and performance benchmarking

name: conduct ICT code review
definition: Review source changes and give actionable technical feedback.

FOUNDATION.text: Distinguish correctness defects from style preferences in a patch
Write actionable feedback tied to an observable risk

INTERMEDIATE.text: Review a feature diff for boundary behavior, tests and maintainability
Prioritize blocking findings and explain suggested corrections

ADVANCED.text: Evaluate cross-cutting design and security risks in a large change
Justify review decisions with evidence and proportionate verification

excludedScope: Writing a new feature and managing Git conflicts

name: Implement responsive layouts
definition: Adapt layout and content to different viewport sizes.

FOUNDATION.text: Explain flexible sizing, flow and viewport-dependent layout
Identify overflow causes in a simple page

INTERMEDIATE.text: Specify a responsive layout across narrow and wide viewports
Preserve content order and usable controls with long text and tables

ADVANCED.text: Evaluate layout strategies for dense data and localization constraints
Define checks for content loss, reflow and interaction stability

excludedScope: Visual brand design and keyboard accessibility verification

name: Use semantic HTML
definition: Choose elements whose meaning matches the content and interaction.

FOUNDATION.text: Choose elements matching headings, navigation and form intent
Explain the difference between a link and an action control

INTERMEDIATE.text: Structure a complex document and form with meaningful relationships
Validate labels, groups and native interaction semantics

ADVANCED.text: Evaluate competing markup structures for reusable components
Justify native-element choices and semantic constraints during composition

excludedScope: CSS layout and custom-widget interaction programming

name: Handle asynchronous web requests
definition: Handle successful responses, HTTP failures and request cancellation in the interface.

FOUNDATION.text: Explain pending, success and failure states of a browser request
Distinguish HTTP failure from a successful empty response

INTERMEDIATE.text: Handle cancellation and stale responses in an interactive search
Specify consistent loading, empty and retry states

ADVANCED.text: Evaluate coordination strategies for overlapping browser operations
Justify freshness and recovery rules under races and intermittent connectivity

excludedScope: Server API design and distributed-message processing

name: Validate application inputs
definition: Enforce input constraints and provide usable validation feedback on client and server.

FOUNDATION.text: Distinguish required, malformed and out-of-range input
Explain why client checks do not replace server validation

INTERMEDIATE.text: Specify consistent validation and feedback at request boundaries
Check nested, missing and adversarial input without trusting the client

ADVANCED.text: Evaluate validation policy across multiple entry points and schema versions
Justify canonicalization and compatibility decisions against ambiguous input

excludedScope: Authorization policy and cryptographic implementation

name: Enforce application authorization
definition: Check permissions for protected actions and resources.

FOUNDATION.text: Distinguish authentication from permission to act on a resource
Identify missing ownership checks in a simple access scenario

INTERMEDIATE.text: Specify trusted actor, organization and resource checks for protected operations
Verify allowed and denied cases including cross-organization access

ADVANCED.text: Evaluate authorization consistency across delegated and asynchronous actions
Justify policy decisions under stale grants and concurrent changes

excludedScope: Identity-provider setup and general authentication implementation

name: Use database transactions
definition: Commit related updates atomically and roll back unsuccessful operations.

FOUNDATION.text: Explain commit and rollback for related database changes
Identify a partial-update failure that violates a business invariant

INTERMEDIATE.text: Define transaction boundaries for a concurrent reservation
Check rollback and competing updates against a stated invariant

ADVANCED.text: Evaluate isolation, lock and retry alternatives under contention
Justify correctness and throughput trade-offs for overlapping transactions

excludedScope: Standalone SQL reporting and distributed consensus

name: Improve existing software structure
definition: Revise existing implementation while checking that required behaviour is preserved.

FOUNDATION.text: Identify duplication and mixed responsibilities in a small function
Explain how characterization checks protect existing behavior

INTERMEDIATE.text: Plan incremental restructuring of a coupled service
Preserve public behavior with focused regression checks

ADVANCED.text: Evaluate alternative decompositions for a legacy subsystem
Justify migration steps and compatibility checks under ongoing change

excludedScope: New business features and architecture replacement

name: Configure continuous integration
definition: Run build and test steps automatically when code changes.

FOUNDATION.text: Explain triggers, jobs and build-test artifacts in a pipeline
Identify how a failing check blocks an unsafe merge

INTERMEDIATE.text: Specify a reproducible build and test workflow for a web application
Handle dependency setup and diagnostic artifacts on failure

ADVANCED.text: Evaluate pipeline isolation, caching and parallelization trade-offs
Justify reliable checks under untrusted changes and constrained runners

excludedScope: Production rollout and infrastructure provisioning
